package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation;

/**
 * Thrown when a create request has the same last name and address as an existing owner and does
 * not opt into sharing a household. Handled by {@link DuplicateHouseholdExceptionHandler}, which
 * responds 409.
 */
public class DuplicateHouseholdException extends Exception {

    public DuplicateHouseholdException(String lastName, String address) {
        super("Owner already exists at this address: " + lastName + ", " + address);
    }
}

## Summary

The `householdId` is now deterministic — the first 12 hex chars of SHA-256 over `(normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode)` — so owners with the same last name and postcode share it automatically.

Changes, kept as small cohesive units to minimize structural impact:

1. **`HouseholdId.java`** (new, small helper — mirrors the existing `IdentityKey`/`CheckDigit` style) — computes the deterministic id from `(lastName, postcode)`, with an overload taking the raw strings so the request path can compute it without an `Owner`.

2. **`Owner.getHouseholdId()`** — reduced to a one-line delegation to `HouseholdId.of(this)`, so the derivation moves out of the large entity class (which also flows into `identityKey`, since that reads `getHouseholdId()`).

3. **`EnsureUniqueHousehold`** — now keys the duplicate block on the computed `householdId` (last name + postcode) instead of last name + address; `sharesHousehold` still bypasses it as a declared member. Wired into `owners.POST.yml` after the identity check, so a second same-household owner gets a **409** unless it opts in.

4. **`PossibleDuplicate`** — added one guard so a same-household owner (equal `householdId`) is never flagged: a declared member is not a suspected duplicate.

`./mvnw -o test` → `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (the new `coreSameLastNameAndPostcodeShareHouseholdId` acceptance test passes), BUILD SUCCESS.

One note on `MembershipLevel`: the spec mentions "the household-size input to the membership level," but the current `MembershipLevel` derives from email presence and namesake count — it has no household-size input to redirect — so nothing there needed changing. Everything that actually keys off the household (`identityKey`, the duplicate block, and `possibleDuplicate`) now uses the computed `householdId`.
